questions.question_text: Given the piecewise function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 4x - 1, & x \le 3 \\ x^{2} - 5, & x > 3 \end{cases}$, which subfunction rule applies to evaluate $f(3)$, and what is its value?

options.why: Substituted into the strict inequality branch $x > 3$ instead of $x \le 3$.
Added $1$ instead of subtracting $1$ when evaluating $4(3) - 1$.
Incorrectly evaluated both subfunctions instead of choosing the single active branch.

questions.question_text: For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} 3x + 2, & x < 0 \\ 2 - x^{2}, & x \ge 0 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(-2)$.

options.why: Substituted into the wrong branch $2 - x^{2}$ to get $2 - (-2)^{2} = -2$.
Subtracted $2$ instead of adding $2$ when evaluating $3(-2) + 2$.
Evaluated the function at the boundary $x = 0$ using $2 - 0^{2} = 2$ instead of at $x = -2$.

questions.question_text: For the function $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} + 2x, & x < 2 \\ 10 - x, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}$, evaluate $f(2)$.

options.why: Substituted into the wrong branch $x^{2} + 2x$ and made an arithmetic error.
Added $x$ instead of subtracting $x$ when evaluating $10 - x$.
Assumed the boundary point is excluded when $x \ge 2$ explicitly includes $x = 2$.

questions.solution_text:
Since $x = 2$ satisfies $x \ge 2$, use the subfunction $10 - x$:
$f(2) = 10 - 2$
$= 8$

questions.question_text:
A function is defined by $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 1, & x < -1 \\ 5, & -1 \le x < 3 \\ 2x - 1, & x \ge 3 \end{cases}$.
Find the value of $f(3)$.

options.why: Substituted into the first branch $2x + 1$ with a sign error.
Substituted $x = 3$ into $2x + 1$ instead of the $x \ge 3$ branch $2x - 1$.
Believed $x = 3$ is not included in the domain.
Read the open circle coordinate at $(1,3)$ instead of the filled dot at $(1,-1)$.
Read the $x$-intercept near $x = 0$ instead of the value at $x = 1$.
Assumed the function is undefined because of the jump discontinuity.

questions.solution_text:
At $x = 1$, locate the filled dot.
The point $(1,3)$ is an open circle (excluded).
The point $(1,-1)$ is a filled dot (included).
$f(1) = -1$

options.why: Read the open circle at $(-2,1)$ instead of the filled circle at $(-2,4)$.
Stated the input $x$-value instead of the output $y$-value.
Read the upper right endpoint coordinate at $x = 2$ instead of $x = -2$.

questions.solution_text:
At $x = -2$, find the included endpoint.
The point $(-2,4)$ has a filled circle.
$g(-2) = 4$

questions.question_text: Given $f(x) = \begin{cases} x^{2} + 1, & x \le 1 \\ 3x - 1, & x > 1 \end{cases}$, calculate the value of $2f(0) + f(3)$.

options.why: Substituted $x = 3$ into the first branch $x^{2} + 1$ to get $10$, then subtracted $2$.
Calculated $f(0) = 2$ instead of $0^{2} + 1 = 1$ before multiplying by $2$.
Omitted the coefficient $2$ on $f(0)$, computing $1 + 8 = 9$ or making an arithmetic error.

questions.solution_text:
Evaluate $f(0)$ using $x^{2} + 1$ (since $0 \le 1$):
$f(0) = 0^{2} + 1 = 1$
Evaluate $f(3)$ using $3x - 1$ (since $3 > 1$):
$f(3) = 3(3) - 1 = 8$
Substitute into the expression:
$2f(0) + f(3) = 2(1) + 8$
$= 2 + 8$
$= 10$

questions.question_text: Given $f(x) = \begin{cases} 2x + 5, & x < 2 \\ x^{2} - 3, & x \ge 2 \end{cases}$, evaluate the nested expression $f(f(1))$.

options.why: Substituted the inner result $7$ into the left branch $2x + 5$ instead of $x^{2} - 3$.
Evaluated only the inner function $f(1) = 7$ without evaluating the outer $f(7)$.
Substituted $x = 1$ into $x^{2} - 3$ to get $-2$, then evaluated $f(-2) = 1$.

questions.solution_text:
First evaluate the inner function $f(1)$ (since $1 < 2$):
$f(1) = 2(1) + 5 = 7$
Now evaluate $f(7)$ with input $x = 7$ (since $7 \ge 2$):
$f(7) = (7)^{2} - 3$
$= 49 - 3$
$= 46$
